prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single, universally “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your crash, the severity of injuries, the insurance situation, and your preferences (trial lawyer vs. settlement-focused firm, language needs, etc.). I can help you find excellent local options, but here’s how to identify the best lawyer for your case and what to do next.

How to pick the right Houston personal injury lawyer
- Look for relevant experience: substantial experience with Texas car-crash cases and serious-injury claims. Trial experience matters if the insurer is likely to fight.
- Board certification: Texas Board of Legal Specialization certification in Personal Injury Trial Law is a strong plus.
- Track record: past verdicts/settlements, especially for cases similar to yours.
- Resources: the firm should have medical experts, accident reconstruction, and the financial ability to advance costs.
- Communication & accessibility: who will handle your file day-to-day, how often you’ll get updates.
- Fee structure: most handle car wrecks on contingency (no fee unless you recover); ask the percentage and which costs are deducted.
- Client reviews & peer recognition: Martindale-Hubbell AV ratings, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Google/Yelp reviews, and local referrals.
- Local reputation: other lawyers, doctors, or consumer groups in Houston can often recommend plaintiff-side trial attorneys.

Questions to ask in an initial consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the results?
- Are you board-certified in personal injury trial law?
- Who will actually handle my case? (Attorney vs. paralegal/junior staff)
- What is your contingency fee and what expenses are my responsibility?
- Do you try cases or primarily settle?
- How long do you expect this will take?
- How will you communicate with me and how often?

Immediate steps after a wreck (if this is recent)
- Get medical care right away and follow doctors’ orders.
- Preserve evidence: photos of scene/vehicles/injuries, police report, contact info for witnesses.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without a lawyer.
- Keep all bills and records (medical, wage loss).
- Report to your insurer as required, but consult a lawyer before accepting a settlement.

If you’d like, I can:
- Search for and give a short list of highly recommended personal injury lawyers/firms in Houston (with credentials, specialties, and contact info).
- Provide sample scripts/questions to use in consultations.
Tell me any preferences (ZIP code or neighborhood, severity of injury, language needs, willingness to go to trial) and I’ll pull a tailored list.
